# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).


---

## Proposal addendum — beat-locked soundtrack and intensity mix (2026-11-17 review)

Accepted as **planned** in the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 6 of
10 of that review's proposals). These requirements are **additive**: they do not
replace any acceptance criterion above.

1. **Beat lock to the shipped lattice.** The music's tempo is the run's
   `beatBpm` (default **80**, 187.5 ms per 16th-note step), not an independent
   tempo. Bars, phrases and transitions align to the *same* lattice every weapon
   already fires on (GDD §2.3), so player shots land on the beat by
   construction. A change to `beatBpm` retunes the music with no other edit, and
   the music can never drift from the fire grid.
2. **Intensity-driven stems, not track swaps.** One continuous musical bed whose
   layers gate on a **documented intensity parameter** derived from game state —
   menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-lives tension, run end — with layer
   entry and exit **on bar boundaries only** (never mid-bar), plus the stinger
   and ducking rules the Audio Design Chapter already defines. The parameter is
   computed from scene state in **one pure helper**, so it is testable,
   reproducible and identical in game and gym.
3. **Never fight the mix.** Music sits under the baked SFX (`docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`),
   carries its own volume separate from the shipped SFX volume/mute settings,
   ducks during boss entrances and power-up fanfares, and degrades to a safe
   no-op without an `AudioContext` — the same contract every shipped cue
   honours.

Why (rationale of record): the game is already rhythmic — every weapon fires on
the silent shared lattice — but the player cannot hear it. Locking music to that
lattice is the cheapest large step in perceived production value and tension,
and it makes the existing fire cadence read as deliberate mastery rather than a
technical detail.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- **AC-M1 — Tempo derived.** A test proves bar and phrase boundaries are
  computed from `beatBpm`, and that changing the tempo moves every boundary with
  it (no hard-coded period anywhere).
- **AC-M2 — Pure intensity, bar-aligned layers.** A test proves the intensity
  parameter is a pure function of the documented state inputs and that every
  layer transition occurs on a bar boundary; the same state sequence produces
  the same transition list.
- **AC-M3 — Mix and safe degradation.** A test proves music never exceeds its
  documented ceiling against the SFX contract, that the no-`AudioContext` path
  is silent and non-throwing, and that music volume is independent of SFX
  volume/mute.

The contract rows for each new state, layer and parameter must be added to the
traceability table owned by **Music contract mapping and traceability guard
(AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3)**.

## Problem statement

The ring-timing CLI's operator-facing text report mixes per-seed and multi-seed
figures. `formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders:

- means over the seed set for `deployments`, `measured runs`, `total`, `banked salvage` and `ring secured`;
- but **seed 1's own value** for `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` (`report.runs[0]?.retryMinutes`, `runs[0]?.betweenSortieMinutes`, `runs[0]?.retakeMinutes` / `runs[0]?.expectedRetakes`).

With the default three-seed evidence set the two halves of one report therefore
describe different populations.

## Evidence

`npm run ring-timing` (2026-11-11, worktree of AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ, exit 0):

```text
Ring 2 · grind · seeds 1, 2, 3
  retries            55.0 min
  total              116.4 min (min 112.7, max 123.4)
```

The committed artefact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, revision
`e873e8c3`) records per-seed `retryMinutes` of **55 / 50 / 55** — a mean of
**53.3**, not 55.0. `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* consequently
quotes "55 of its 116.4 min (≈47 %)", pairing seed 1's retry total with the
mean total (the mean-based share is ≈45.8 %). `between sorties` and
`exposed re-capture` happen to be seed-invariant today, so only the retry line
is visibly wrong — but the rendering is one bug, not one line.

## Expected behaviour

Every metric line in the text report describes the same population (the seed
set), consistent with the JSON artefact: mean plus min–max for the per-run
totals, or an explicitly labelled seed-1 sample. The report-rendering test
(`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` § *report rendering*) should pin a
multi-seed case where the seeds differ, so the mixing cannot return.

## Acceptance criteria

- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the multi-seed aggregate (mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it), or labels them as a single seed; no line silently reports seed 1 as the seed-set figure.
- A report-rendering test feeds a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ and asserts the rendered value is the mean, not seed 1's.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* quotes the retry minutes and share from the aggregate consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact.
- Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Found by the verification slice `Record the ring 2 before/after split and verify the acceptance criteria (AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ)`; deliberately not fixed there (that item's scope forbids code changes).
- No behaviour or measured value changes: this is a reporting/consistency fix only.

- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** – Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured 48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window (open)
- **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X** – Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min vs the authored 40–60 min window (open)
- **AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL** – Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, asserts, banked, based (+119 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, asserts, banked, based (+109 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, artefact, asserts, based (+104 more)
## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-14)

Four children, test-first dependency order (3 planned + 1 auto-closed coverage gap):

1. **Test: report rendering pins multi-seed retry aggregates (AH-0MWGVXB95002W7KI)** — task, low. Pins parent AC 2: a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ must render the aggregate mean, never seed 1's; also pins the between-sorties and exposed-re-capture lines.
2. **Implement: render retry/between-sortie/recapture from the seed aggregate (AH-0MWGVXJ5V008QV50)** — bug, low. Adds `betweenSortieMinutes` / `retryMinutes` / `retakeMinutes` / `expectedRetakes` `RingTimingStats` to `RingTimingSummary`, renders the three report lines from the aggregates in `formatRingTimingReport`, and regenerates the committed baseline artefact (deterministic; additive summary fields). Depends on 1.
3. **Docs: EVALUATION.md retry share from the aggregate (AH-0MWGVXRFS009HBR5)** — docs, low. Quotes the retry minutes + share from the aggregate in `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline*, consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact. Depends on 2.
4. **Close coverage gap: Full project test suite passes. (AH-0MWGW08C0006CDUX)** — task, medium, auto-created by the AC coverage review; verifies the full suite via the test skill at the dev-push gate.

Vertical slicing: each phase is a thin end-to-end slice (test → code + evidence → docs); the scope is Small, so no further phasing is needed.

- 2026-11-15: plan re-run (idempotent, post-implement-drive stop) — plan already complete: 4 children in test-first dependency order with edges wired (test -> implement -> docs -> coverage-gap); coverage review re-verified (proceed, 100%, triage items excluded); parent restored to `plan_complete`; no new children or plan blocks created.

Rationale: every other report line is already aggregate and the JSON artefact is the stated consistency reference. Final: aggregate extension.
- A2 (artefact): regenerate `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` so its JSON summary carries the new fields. Deterministic per the existing determinism test; existing mean/min/max totals must be unchanged. Final: regenerate.

# Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min against the authored 40–60 min window

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V (Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing
items), part of the re-measurement chain under AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A (Re-measure
ring timing for one-level hex deployments). **Producer ruling required** — this
item records the evidence and the options; it does not decide which way the
budget should move.

## Why this item exists

`RING_TIMING_TARGETS` authors ring 1's grind window as **40–60 minutes** with a
±10 % tolerance of the window's width (**±2 minutes**), judged on the **grind**
line. The regenerated artifact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, produced
by `AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02` from the shipped code) measures the shipped one-level
five-wave sortie at **16.4 minutes**, so the authored window no longer holds.
The parent's acceptance criteria forbid silently re-wording a missed budget,
so the miss is recorded here and the ruling is left to the producer.

## Measurement (source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, ring 1, `grind`, seeds 1–3)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **missed** (`withinWindow: false`, `withinTolerance: false`) |
| Measured total mean | **16.4256 min** (seeds: 15.7239 / 16.6383 / 16.9144) |
| Measured total min–max | **15.7239 – 16.9144 min** |
| Authored window | **40 – 60 min** |
| Tolerance | ±10 % of window width = **±2 min** (tolerance floor 38 min) |
| Delta to window floor | **−23.5744 min** below 40 min; **−21.5744 min** below the 38 min tolerance floor |
| Deployment minutes (measured, mean) | 2.2128 (1.8619 / 2.3192 / 2.4572) |
| Between-sortie minutes (modelled) | 12.0 (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Retry minutes (measured replay) | 2.2128 (= the replayed deployment's measured length) |
| Re-capture minutes (modelled) | 0.0 (the grind line secures the ring) |
| Split check | 2.2128 + 12.0 + 2.2128 + 0.0 = 16.4256 = the total mean |
| Captured / lost sorties | 0.0 / **6.0** per run — every sortie is a first-attempt loss to enemy fire and is retried |
| Ring secured | 3 / 3 runs (the grind plays every hex, so the ring still ends secured) |
| Salvage | 0.0 banked, 15.0 forfeited (mean: 25 / 4 / 16) |

## Before/after attributable to the one-level model

| Ring 1 grind | Before (campaign slice) | After (one-level sortie) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total mean (min–max) | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | **16.4 (15.7–16.9)** | −37.9 min |
| Verdict | in-window (40–60) | **missed (40–60)** | window no longer holds |
| Deployment minutes | 19.0 | 2.2 | −16.8 (the slice no longer climbs campaign levels past the hex's own) |
| Retry minutes | 23.3 | 2.2 | −21.1 (retry now charges the replayed deployment's measured length, not a flat 5 min) |
| Between-sortie minutes | 12.0 | 12.0 | unchanged (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Re-capture minutes | 0.0 | 0.0 | unchanged on the grind line |
| Captured / lost | 1.3 / 4.7 | 0.0 / 6.0 | no sortie clears under the per-level arena's fire-on fidelity |
| Salvage banked / forfeited | 24.0 / 54.0 | 0.0 / 15.0 | no capture ⇒ no banking |

The dominant driver is the deployment model itself: a deployment's measured
arena time fell from ≈3.2 min to ≈0.4 min, and the retry term follows it
mechanically (retry = the replayed deployment's measured length). The
between-sortie allowance (2 min) and the re-capture allowance are unchanged and
do not drive the delta.

## Options (for the producer; not a recommendation)

1. **Re-author the ring-1 window** (e.g. from 40–60 min to a window the shipped
   one-level model measures). Cheapest, but it changes the design of record
   (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape) rather than the game.
2. **Tune the authored ring data** — more hexes in ring 1, or higher
   aggression/level per hex — so a ring-1 clear takes the authored time. This
   changes gameplay pace, not the timing model.
3. **Revisit the allowances** — the between-sortie 2 minutes, the retry rule
   (one modelled replay per loss) and the rush re-capture charge. A larger
   between-sortie or retry allowance would lengthen the measured total, but it
   prices a deployment time the harness does not measure.
4. **Revisit the measurement boundary** — the per-level arena ignores the wave
   `shootEnabled` gate, so every sortie is lost to enemy fire and none is
   captured. Honouring the gate (or modelling the mini-boss encounter, also
   unmodelled) would raise captures and change the measured total; that is a
   harness/model decision (`AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM` chain), not a budget re-word.

## Acceptance criteria

- The producer rules on one of the options (or another) and records the
  decision on this item; **no option is taken implicitly** by a later code or
  docs change.
- If the ruling re-authors the window, `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the docs guards
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) and
  the quoted documents are updated together and the artifact re-judged.
- If the ruling tunes the ring data or the allowances, the artifact is
  regenerated with the documented command and the before/after evidence is
  recorded here.
- Whatever the ruling, ring 1's grind verdict is stated honestly (measured
  figure, window, delta) — never re-worded as passing.
- The full project test suite passes with the change.

`discovered-from:AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V`,
`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`
(`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape.

- **AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL** – Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (completed)

# Fade bullets out

## Problem statement

When an enemy bullet reaches the end of its range (its lifetime expires), it
currently **pops out of existence** — its sprite is destroyed in one frame.
Instead it should **shrink to nothing** during the last 20 % of its life, so
the expiry reads as a smooth visual dissolve rather than a snap. The bullet
remains dangerous while it shrinks.

## Users

- **Players** — as a player, I want enemy bullets to shrink away smoothly as
  they exhaust their range, so the game feel is polished and bullet expiry is
  readable at a glance instead of popping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Shrink over the last 20 %:** an enemy bullet's view scales down
  from its full size to nothing during the final 20 % of its lifetime, and is
  destroyed when the lifetime elapses (as today).
- **AC2 — Full size before the fade window:** before the last 20 % of its
  lifetime the bullet renders at full scale (unchanged behaviour for the
  stored/lifetime bulk of its flight).
- **AC3 — Damages the player while shrinking:** the bullet's collision
  footprint keeps tracking its **visual sprite bounds** during the fade — it
  can still hit the player while visibly smaller, exactly until it fades away
  entirely.
- **AC4 — Enemy bullets only:** player bullets are **not** affected — their
  existing expiry behaviour is unchanged.
- **AC5 — Shared seam, gym↔game parity:** the change lands in the shared
  enemy-bullet lifecycle (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`), so the game
  and every gym scene that spawns enemy bullets fade identically; gyms that
  exercise enemy bullets cover the new behaviour.
- **AC6 — Testing:** automated unit tests verify the fade-window scaling
  (including a bullet destroyed exactly at expiry), no scaling outside the
  window, and that an animated (`redraw`) bullet fades too without regressing
  the per-frame animation hook.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Enemy bullets shrink smoothly to nothing as their range runs out instead of
popping away, while staying just as dangerous while they fade.

## Constraints

- The shared lifecycle helper `advanceWrappingBullets` is the single
  ownership point for enemy-bullet advance, wrap and expiry — every scene
  (game and gyms) consumes it, so behaviour must not diverge per scene
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1, gym↔game parity).
- The bullet view is now a **sprite of a cached texture**, not a Graphics
  object (AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF); scaling must go through the sprite's
  `setScale` (no per-frame redraw of the texture).
- Fade duration is **not** proportional to bullet size — it is a fixed
  20 % of the bullet's own lifetime (producer decision, Q3).
- The existing expiry must still destroy the sprite exactly when the
  lifetime elapses (tested by the current suite).
- Collision/hitbox: enemy bullets currently use a fixed radius
  (`getEnemyBulletRadius`, ~8 px); the fade must make the effective
  footprint follow the visual sprite bounds while shrinking (producer
  decision, Q5).

## Risks & assumptions

- The bullet view contract (`BulletView`) must gain a scale capability;
  every consumer — game, gyms and the test stub — needs the new member.
  Mitigation: extend the structural interface and the `StubEnemyBullet` in
  `bulletLifecycle.test.ts` in the same change (the test already drives the
  shape of the contract).
- Scale baseline assumption: full scale (1.0) is the bullet's baked sprite
  size; the fade interpolates from 1.0 to ~0 over the window regardless of
  the baked radius — no radius-proportional formula (producer decision Q3).
- Collision-footprint change must not regress the fixed-radius path for
  bullets outside the fade window (AC2) nor the bomb/clearing paths that
  iterate `getEnemyBullets()` (PlayScene 3532, 1792).
- Scope-creep guard: fade applies to enemy bullets only; anything further
  (e.g. player-bullet fades, alpha fades, radius-proportional timing) is
  recorded as a separate work item, not part of this one.

## Existing state

In `advanceWrappingBullets` (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`), each
enemy bullet advances, wraps at the four edges, optionally animates through
its `redraw` hook, and is destroyed the moment `elapsed >= lifetime` — the
sprite vanishes in one frame. Enemy-bullet collision against the player uses
`getEnemyBulletRadius()` in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`.

## Desired change

Inside `advanceWrappingBullets`, once the bullet enters its final 20 % of
lifetime, scale its view down smoothly from full size to zero (e.g. linearly
with the remaining time fraction) before destroying it at expiry. The
shrink must be observable through the same structural view contract every
scene and test uses, and the collision footprint must shrink with the visual.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — `advanceWrappingBullets` (+ the
  `WrappingBullet` / `BulletView` structural interfaces; likely add a
  `setScale` capability to the view contract) — owns the fade-window scaling.
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — unit tests for the fade
  window, no-scaling-outside-window, animated-bullet fade, expiry-at-zero.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `getEnemyBulletRadius()` /
  enemy-bullet-vs-player collision — make the hit radius track the fading
  sprite bounds.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/…` — consumers of
  `advanceWrappingBullets`; verify parity (no per-scene copies to change).
- `docs/…` — GDD §4.4 (bullet range/lifetime) / any visual-feel docs, if
  the fade deserves a mention.

## Related work

- AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 — Bullets have a distance and wrap around the screen
  (lifetime/expiry model this builds on; completed).
- AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF — Cache bullet shapes as textures and batch bullet
  draw submission (sprite-of-cached-texture view; completed).
- AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA — shared bullet-lifecycle extraction parent
  (the helper this changes; completed).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (shared seam
  requirement; completed).
- AH-0MVT2W5EL004OXNN — Eval arena wrap parity (bullet lifetime expiry
  preserved; completed).
- AH-0MUL15N63003PUDB — Animate enemies gliding to their re-anchored
  formation slots (smooth-motion/tweening precedent; completed).
- AH-0MV70Y2XY005J2HI — Hold-full overlay: fade the thruster/engine hum out
  while paused (fade precedent; completed).

### Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (imported into this brief): repository
keyword matches in `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (bullets/damage/range/fade/shrink
terms). Full report:
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MWJ9PMYF005N588.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — Fade mechanism: reduce alpha, scale, or both? — Answer (producer):
  **scale only**. Research: cached-texture sprites support `setScale`
  directly (AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF); alpha fades are used elsewhere (pulse
  wave §7.2) but the producer chose shrink-by-scale for bullets.
- Q2 — When does the fade begin? — Answer (producer): **the last 20 % of
  the bullet's life**. Fixed fraction of lifetime, not a fixed time.
- Q3 — Fade duration proportional to initial size? — Answer (producer):
  **ignore** — stick to the last 20 % of life for every bullet regardless of
  size. Note: this supersedes the original description's "duration of the
  shrink should be proportional to their initial size". Prior
  answer/description text updated in this brief.
- Q4 — Player bullets? — Answer (producer): **enemy only**.
- Q5 — Hitbox during the fade — Answer (producer): **visual sprite bounds**;
  the bullet can still damage the player while shrinking, exactly until it
  fades to nothing.

# Make hex strengths and weaknesses mean something in combat

## Problem statement

As a player reading the hex map, I want the **STRENGTHS / WEAKNESSES** lines to
change how the fight actually goes, so the intel is a decision I can act on
rather than a label I can ignore.

Today those lines are **inert display text**. They are authored
(`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, e.g. `strengths: ['cannon','dual']`,
`weaknesses: ['nova','arc']`), validated only as "non-empty array of non-empty
strings" (`validateRingDefinitions`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts:415`), and
copied verbatim into the detail panel (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts:964-965`,
`:1082-1083`) which `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` draws for `HexMapScene` and
`GymHexWar`. **No runtime rule reads them**: not the defence resolver
(`resolveDefence`), not the run's boss profile (`HexBossProfile`,
`src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts:102` — it takes the hex id, aggression, authored
boss name, grant and personality, never strengths/weaknesses), not the capture
cycle, not the hangar economy, not attract traversal. Bringing the "weakness"
weapon gives no bonus; bringing a "strength" weapon costs nothing.

So the design's own promise is unkept — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md:1021`
("the strategist … boss's strengths and weaknesses") and
`docs/Game Design Document.md:2831` ("Boss and weapon strength are known
ahead"), both of which assume the information is *mechanically* load-bearing.

## Users (with example user stories)

- **The strategist** — "I read that a hex's boss is weak to `nova`; I want
  bringing `nova` to visibly and measurably tear through it, and bringing the
  weapon it is strong against to feel like shooting a wall, so my pre-deployment
  reading pays off."
- **The grinder** — "I want a wrong-loadout attempt to be *legible* — I should
  hear and see that my weapon is the problem within seconds, not discover it at
  the third phase of the mini-boss."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "I must be able to read effectiveness
  without relying on colour alone."
- **The implementer/gym user** — "I want the same matchup rule and the same
  feedback in the game and in the gyms, from one shared seam."

## Proposed approaches (Q1 answered: A + B; Q4 answered: lists authoritative — see Decisions)

All five deliver "the right weapon is significantly better, the wrong weapon is
significantly worse". They differ in cost, legibility and balance risk. Shared
plumbing (weapon identity on the shot, a hex→run hand-off and one feedback
seam) is common to A/B/C/E; the juice requirements below apply to whichever is
chosen.

### A — Hit-charge multiplier on the one hit seam *(recommended core)*

The authored lists **become the rule**: `weaknesses` = weapons that counter this
boss, `strengths` = weapons it resists. One pure resolver
(`resolveHexMatchup(weaponId, definition) → 'effective' | 'neutral' |
'resisted'`) maps a shot to a **hit charge**: `effective` = 2 hit points per
connected shot, `resisted` = 1 hit point per **two** connected shots (a
per-target ledger keyed by weapon, so the cost is bounded and deterministic),
`neutral` = 1.

- **Why it fits the engine:** the game is a hit-count model — `takeDamage()`
  takes no argument and one call is one hit point
  (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:543`, `MiniBoss.takeDamage`
  `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts:347`), and `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet`
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:555`) is the **single** seam every player
  damage source funnels through (bullets, damage-budget beams, AOE). Multiplying
  the charge there means one rule, not one rule per weapon.
- **Player legibility:** high — two-hit-per-shot reads instantly on a
  multi-hit boss, and "every other shot is shrugged off" reads as resistance.
- **Effort:** S–M. **Balance risk:** medium (it moves time-to-kill, hence ring
  timing). **Rounding** at the resisted rate is the main cost: it needs a small
  ledgers module and a stated tie rule.

### B — Deflect gate for the wrong weapon *(strongest juice, can layer on A)*

Resisted hits are **physically deflected**: the shot is consumed, deals nothing,
and produces a distinct metal clang, a spark shower off the boss's armour rim
and a visible ricochet. Effective hits get a "critical" family (bright shard
burst, pitched-up cue, boss recoil).

- **Player legibility:** highest — the player sees shots bouncing off.
- **Risk:** a high deflect rate is frustrating; the counter-play must be
  advertised (map panel + HUD glyph) so it reads as "wrong tool", never as a
  broken gun.

### C — Weapon damage types (energy / kinetic / explosive)

Introduce damage types, map every catalogue weapon to a type, and author per-hex
resistance/vulnerability per type; the existing `strengths`/`weaknesses` strings
become *derived* display (validated against the type table) instead of
authoritative.

- **Ceiling:** highest — one table tunes every future hex and boss.
- **Effort:** L (weapon catalogue, CSV seeds + parity tests, balance docs, ring
  timing, gym parity). Worth it only if the matchup system is expected to grow
  beyond two lists per hex.

### D — Advisory-only (no combat maths change) *(cheap non-answer; recorded for completeness)*

Keep damage untouched and make the intel load-bearing another way: the
deployment selector shows a projected kill-speed per owned weapon for the chosen
hex, and (optionally) pre-selects the counter weapon. Effort S, no balance risk
— but it does **not** deliver the requested handicap, and is essentially today's
behaviour plus polish. Not recommended as the answer to this item.

### E — Weakness stagger meter *(mechanic rather than multiplier; possible follow-up)*

Matching-damage builds a stagger meter; filling it opens a damage window (boss
stunned, larger VFX/SFX reward, bonus damage). Non-matching damage builds a
resistance meter instead, plating the boss. More texture than 2×/0.5×, more
moving parts (a new boss-attached state machine, gym surface, HUD).

| | Legibility | Effort | Balance risk | Testability | Fits existing seams |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A hit-charge | High | S–M | Medium | High (pure resolver + seam test) | Very high — one seam |
| B deflect gate | Highest | M | Medium | High | High — one seam + impact spec |
| C damage types | High | L | Medium–High | High | Medium — catalogue-wide |
| D advisory | Medium | S | None | High | High, but no rule |
| E stagger | High | M–L | Medium | Medium | Medium — new boss state |

**Chosen (producer decision, session 2026-11-17): A + B.** Approach **A is
the rule** — the authored lists stay authoritative and the advantage/handicap is
a resolved hit charge applied at the single hit seam — and **B is the
presentation of the resisted state**: a strength-weapon shot is *physically
deflected* (consumed, no damage, metal clang, spark shower off the armour rim,
visible ricochet), while an effective shot gets the distinct "critical" family
(bright shard burst, pitched-up cue, boss recoil). C and E are recorded as
follow-ups, not part of this item; D is rejected as the answer.

The MVP therefore delivers: one pure rule (A), one unmistakable in-run read
(B), and the tune still lives in authored data.

## The juice is part of the acceptance, not a polish pass

Whichever approach is chosen, the player must be able to tell which state they
are in **without reading a number**:

- **Effective (counter weapon):** brighter/larger impact flash in the boss's
  weakness colour; the existing hit cue **pitched up** (`playCue` already takes
  `{ rate }`, `src/audio/effects.ts:1176-1187`) plus one added harmonic/shatter
  layer; boss **flinch** (small positional kick + white silhouette flash); a
  visibly larger chunk off the phase health bar with a bigger tween; optional
  brief hit-stop/zoom pulse, bounded so dense fire never stutters.
- **Resisted (strength weapon):** dull, low, short cue at a reduced rate; a
  **grey armour flash riding the boss silhouette** rather than a bright hit
  flash; spall/deflect particles (a shard or dull ring — never the bright shard
  burst); **no flinch**; a small "resisted" pip on the health bar; a one-shot
  "RESISTED" tag on the first resisted hit of the encounter (never per hit).
- **Neutral:** byte-for-byte today's per-weapon behaviour (existing
  `impactFx` spec path, `src/utils/weapons.ts:~1016`,
  `CombatScene.resolveImpactFx` `:627`).
- **Never colour-only** (CVD policy precedent: `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`):
  each state pairs colour with a distinct **shape** (shard burst vs. dull ring
  vs. splinter) and a distinct **pitch**, so state is readable with colour
  vision deficiency and with sound alone.
- **Pre-commitment readability:** the hex detail panel marks each listed weapon
  with the glyph it will show in combat (e.g. `▲ effective` / `▼ resisted`) and
  the deployment/loadout selector shows the same glyph on owned weapons against
  the selected hex, so the intel and the in-run feedback use one vocabulary.
- **Audio must be baked through the existing pipeline** (ToneForge export +
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` mapping), not synthesised ad-hoc in a
  scene, and routed through the one shared impact dispatcher
  (`playWeaponImpactCue`, `src/audio/effects.ts:815`).

## Decisions

- **Q1 — Which approach? — ANSWERED: A + B.** A's hit-charge multiplier is the
  rule; B's deflect gate is how the *resisted* state presents, and the
  effective state gets the matching "critical" family (bright shard burst,
  pitched-up cue, boss flinch). Decided by the producer in this session; recorded
  in the comment log on this item. Approach C (damage types) and E (stagger
  meter) are linked follow-up candidates, not scope here; D is rejected.
- **Q2 — Scope of the multiplier — ANSWERED: mini-boss and elites.** Decided by
  the producer (2026-11-17). "Elites" is defined concretely as **every enemy
  whose configured hit pool is greater than one** (`health` in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, e.g. Harvester = 5) **plus the deployment's
  wave-5 `MiniBoss`**. Ordinary chaff (`health` = 1, destroyed by any hit)
  resolves **neutrally** — a multiplier cannot make a one-hit enemy more
  fragile, and a resisted chaff hit would double its time-to-kill for no
  legibility gain. The boss is where the intel pays off, and this keeps the
  rebalance contained (AC12's ring-timing measurement is still required because
  the mini-boss is what ends a deployment).
- **Q3 — Magnitudes — ANSWERED: ×2 / ×0.5.** Decided by the producer
  (2026-11-17). Effective = **two hit points per connected shot**; resisted =
  **one hit point per two connected shots** (bounded per-target ledger).
  Never immune, and a wrong loadout stays winnable. No per-hex override in the
  MVP — a tuned CSV magnitude is a follow-up, not scope here.
- **Q4 — Authoring shape — ANSWERED: (a) the authored lists stay authoritative.**
  Decided by the producer (2026-11-17) after reading the briefing in
  *Appendix — Q4 briefing: authored lists vs damage types* below. The resolver's
  **input is shaped as a verdict lookup for a weapon id** (not a direct list
  scan), so approach C's type-derived default — or the per-hex override hybrid —
  can land later behind the same seam with no change to the combat code, the
  impact-feedback seam or the state→cue/spec tests. Damage types are a linked
  follow-up, not scope here.
- **Q5 — Normalisation — ANSWERED: normalise as proposed.** Decided by the
  producer (2026-11-17). The authored `strengths`/`weaknesses` are normalised to
  catalogue weapon ids (camelCase `waveLaser` → `wave_laser`, through one shared
  mapping like `resolveHexGrant`), and validation fails loudly at load on an id
  that resolves to no catalogue weapon or a weapon in **both** lists of the same
  hex.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl show` records the producer's answers to **all** decisions (Q1 answered:
   A + B; Q2–Q5 still open at the time of writing), and the implementation
   matches them — Q1's A-rule/B-presentation split is visible in where the rule
   lives (pure resolver at the hit seam) and where the deflect presentation
   lives (impact-feedback seam).
2. A **pure, headless** matchup resolver lives in `src/core/hangarWar/` and is
   the only place the advantage/handicap is decided; unit-tested for
   `effective` / `neutral` / `resisted`, for an **unknown weapon id** (neutral,
   total) and for an **unauthored hex** (neutral). Its input is a **verdict
   lookup for a weapon id** (Q4 = a), not a direct scan of the authored lists,
   so a type-derived default can be introduced later without touching the combat
   seam (asserted by the resolver's unit tests taking a supplied lookup).
3. The authored `strengths`/`weaknesses` are **normalised to catalogue weapon
   ids** and validated: an id that resolves to no catalogue weapon, or a weapon
   that appears in **both** lists of the same hex, fails loudly at load
   (`validateRingDefinitions` or its successor), with a test per failure mode.
   (No shipped hex currently has such an overlap; the guard is for authoring.)
4. The resolved matchup reaches the run **through the existing hex→run
   hand-off** (`HexBossProfile` → `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel`), so the game, the
   attract run and every gym read one value — no scene re-derives it.
5. Every player damage source honours the multiplier: ordinary bullets,
   damage-budget beams (wave laser), AOE detonations and the per-matchup ledger
   share the one rule; a test proves each source is affected identically.
6. **Measured effect:** against the same mini-boss phase, the effective weapon
   kills **at least 1.8× faster** and the resisted weapon **at least 1.8×
   slower** than the neutral weapon, asserted in a headless test with the
   chosen magnitudes (so the numbers are pinned, not prose).
7. **Felt effect (SFX):** effective and resisted states play **different cues at
   different playback rates** than neutral, the cues exist in the ToneForge cue
   map, and a test asserts the state→cue mapping; no state is silent.
8. **Felt effect (VFX):** effective and resisted states spawn **different
   impact specs** (colour *and* shape, not colour alone), and a test asserts the
   state→spec mapping plus that neutral is byte-identical to today's per-weapon
   `impactFx`.
9. **Non-flinch/flinch asymmetry:** the boss shows a visible reaction to an
   effective hit and **none** to a resisted hit (testable through a
   published/animated reaction flag rather than pixel diffing).
10. **CVD/audio-only readability:** each state is distinguishable by shape and
    by pitch with colour removed, and the hex map's detail panel publishes the
    same glyph vocabulary it will show in combat (shipped-data test).
11. **Gym↔game parity:** `GymBoss` (or a dedicated gym surface) can toggle the
    three states and shows identical damage, cue and VFX behaviour to the game;
    a parity test covers the mapping.
12. **Balance is re-measured, not assumed:** `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` is
    re-run with the matchup rule in play, the ring-1/ring-2 measurements are
    recorded on this item, and any tuned constant is documented in
    `docs/BALANCING.md`; if ring timing moves outside its derived window, the
    rebalance is either applied here or filed as a linked follow-up item.
13. **Docs:** GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` and the hex-map intel
    docs state what strengths/weaknesses now *do* (with the chosen magnitudes),
    and remove the current "advisory only" implication.
14. **Nothing survives that would block approach C later:** the resolver's
    verdict lookup is injectable and tested with a synthetic lookup (no authored
    data), proving the rule is decoupled from the lists' storage — a follow-up
    can swap the lookup's backing table for a damage-type table without editing
    `CombatScene` or the impact seam.
15. Full project test suite passes (via the test skill, at the dev-push gate).

## Impact

The hex map's strengths and weaknesses become a real pre-deployment decision:
the counter weapon visibly tears a boss apart (brighter, sharper, higher-pitched
hits and a boss that flinches) while the weapon the boss is strong against
clangs off its armour and barely scratches it, so the intel finally pays for the
reading.

## Constraints

- **One rule, one seam.** The matchup must resolve in a pure module and apply
  through the existing hit seam (`CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet`) and the
  existing feedback seam (`resolveImpactFx` / per-weapon `impactFx`), never as a
  per-scene or per-entity special case (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- **Determinism.** No new randomness and no new consumption of the seeded RNG
  stream: a replay of the same payload/seed must land the same hits.
- **Authored data stays the tune.** Magnitudes and any per-hex override live in
  authored data / CSV seeds with the repo's parity test, not in scene constants.
- **A wrong loadout is winnable.** Resist, never immune; the handicap must not
  make a hex unwinnable with the only weapons a player owns.
- **Existing saves keep working.** Any new persisted field is optional and
  field-presence migratable (the established pattern in
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`).
- **No balance-by-vibes.** Ring timing and the balance docs are the measurement
  of record.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — balance blast radius.** A global multiplier rebalances every weapon
  against every enemy. Mitigation: Q2 scope (mini-boss + elites) and AC12's
  re-measurement.
- **Risk — the resisted state reads as a bug** ("my gun stopped working").
  Mitigation: the deflect/armour presentation plus the pre-commitment glyph and
  HUD tag; a wrong weapon must still *look* like it is hitting something.
- **Risk — noise.** Per-hit critical/resist text would clutter a bullet-hell
  screen. Mitigation: one-shot "RESISTED" tag per encounter, bar pips
  thereafter.
- **Risk — rounding at the resisted rate.** "Every other shot" is coarse.
  Mitigation: a deterministic per-target ledger with the tie rule stated in the
  resolver's docs and tests.
- **Assumption —** the lists are the right source of truth (they already read
  as weapon ids and are authored per hex); no new taxonomy is needed for A/B/E.
- **Assumption —** the engine's hit-count model can express a 2×/0.5× matchup
  without touching `takeDamage()`'s contract (two calls, or a ledger) — verified
  by AC5/AC6 tests before any global balance work.
- **Assumption —** the audio pipeline can host new cue variants without a
  re-bake of every existing weapon cue (one new family per state, existing cues
  pitch-shifted at the call site).

## Appendix — Q4 briefing: authored lists vs damage types

Written to answer the producer's Q4 question ("explain what this means and the
implications of each choice; which is most flexible vs most work"). 18 authored
hexes, 16 catalogue weapons, and the shipped lists currently name only **9** of
those 16 (`cannon, dual, spread, rapid, waveLaser, ricochet, nova, mortar,
arc`) — the other seven (`cluster, options, rear_guard, broadside, railgun,
shard_swarm, heavy_slug`) are neutral against every boss today and would stay
neutral unless authored.

### (a) The authored lists stay authoritative *(per weapon, per hex)*

`weaknesses` = counters, `strengths` = resisted, resolved by weapon id.

- **Granularity:** finest — "this boss resists `ricochet` but not `spread`" is
  expressible; designers can encode one-off counters (`nova` wrecks the leviathan)
  without inventing a taxonomy.
- **Migration cost:** **zero**. The data already exists, is mirrored in
  `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` with a parity test, and already displays.
  Work is limited to Q5's normalisation + validation and the resolver itself.
- **Growth cost — the real weakness:** an unlisted weapon is **silently
  neutral**. Ship a new weapon next month and it is neutral against all 18 hexes,
  and *no test can fail*, because "neutral" is a legal value. Authoring burden
  grows as hexes × relevant weapons.
- **Flexibility today:** highest. **Work:** lowest.

### (b) Derive from weapon damage types *(per type, per hex)*

Every weapon gets a type (energy / kinetic / explosive / beam — note the repo
already groups `nova, mortar, arc` as the "AOE family", so a taxonomy has
precedent); each hex authors a resisted type and a vulnerable type; the panel's
`STRENGTHS:`/`WEAKNESSES:` lines are **generated** from the table, so the
displayed text can never drift from the rule.

- **Granularity:** coarser — all kinetic weapons behave alike against a boss.
  Recovering the lost expressiveness means inventing more types, which converges
  back toward (a) with an extra indirection.
- **Growth cost — the real strength:** a new weapon = **one** type assignment
  and it *inherits* every existing boss relationship (no silent neutral); a new
  hex = two cells. Completeness is loudly checkable: "every catalogue weapon has
  a type" is a total test, and a hex with no posture can be a load-time error.
- **Migration cost:** highest — rewrite 18 hex rows + both CSV seeds + parity
  tests, regenerate the panel copy, update GDD §8.2 and
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, and make judgement calls on ~16 weapons
  (is `arc` energy or explosive?). Balance re-measurement is required either way
  (AC12).
- **Flexibility for content growth:** highest. **Work:** highest (L vs S–M), and
  it delays shipping A+B.

### (c) Hybrid — types as the default, per-hex weapon overrides

Type gives a weapon's default verdict; a hex may override a specific weapon.
Maximum flexibility, but it is **both jobs**. It can be staged, which is why the
recommendation below is (a) now and (c) later: choose (a), but shape the
resolver's input as *a verdict lookup for a weapon id* so the type-derived
default can be introduced behind the same seam later, with no change to the
combat code, the impact seam or the tests that pin the state→cue/spec mapping.

| | (a) lists | (b) types | (c) hybrid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expressiveness today | highest | lower | highest |
| Cost to ship with A+B | **lowest** | highest | high |
| Cost per new weapon | hexes × new pairing (silent neutral) | **one cell, inherited** | one cell |
| Silent-neutral risk | **high** | low | low |
| Loud validation possible | partial (ids, overlap) | **full (completeness)** | full |
| Migration | none | 18 rows + CSVs + docs | both |
| Delays A+B | no | yes | yes |

**Recommendation for Q4: (a)** — the choice that ships A+B soonest, reuses
authored data that already exists, and loses nothing permanently if the resolver
takes a verdict lookup as its input (so (c) remains open for later).

## Appendix — evidence gathered while writing this item

- Intel display path: `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts:938` (`hexLabel`), `:964-965`
  (panel lines), `:1082-1083` (published fields), constants at `:244-245`; drawn
  by `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`; gym copy at
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts:347`.
- Validation: `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts:415` — non-empty strings only.
- No runtime consumer: a `src/`-wide search (excluding tests, the definitions,
  the intel model and the gym display) finds only comments.
- Runtime hand-off for a deployment: `HexBossProfile`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts:102`, built by `buildHexBossProfile` `:360`)
  → `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel` (`src/waves/miniBossDesigns.ts:362`) → `MiniBoss`.
- Hit seam: `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:555`);
  feedback seam: `resolveWeaponImpactFx` `:613` / `resolveImpactFx` `:627`;
  per-weapon spec `ImpactFxSpec` (`src/utils/weapons.ts:~1016`).
- `PlayerBullet` carries `impactFx` but **no weapon id**
  (`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts:115`, factory `:363`) — identity must be
  plumbed or the matchup baked onto the shot at fire time.
- Audio: `playWeaponImpactCue` (`src/audio/effects.ts:815`) over
  `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`; `playCue(name, { rate })` support
  (`:1176-1187`); 15 per-weapon impact cues already baked
  (`playCannonImpactSound` `:651` … `playWaveLaserImpactSound` `:1065`).
- Per-weapon VFX already ships: impact flash colour/radius/duration, muzzle
  flash, bullet trail/flame (`MuzzleFlashSpec` / `ImpactFxSpec`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts:~988-1016`); impact flash spawner
  `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`.
- Id mismatch: definitions use `waveLaser`, catalogue uses `wave_laser`
  (`src/utils/weapons.ts:1263`); `resolveHexGrant` normalises grants
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts:742`), the strength/weakness lists are untouched.
- Shipped authoring: `strengths`/`weaknesses` across rings 1–2 draw from
  `cannon, dual, spread, rapid, waveLaser, ricochet, nova, mortar, arc`; no
  shipped hex lists the same weapon in both lists (verified) — so an
  overlap guard breaks nothing today.
- Design intent: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md:1021-1048,1119` and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md:2831` frame the intel as a strategist
  affordance that the current build never cashes.
- Measurement of record: `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` (plays the shipped
  five-wave deployment per hex) and `docs/BALANCING.md`.


---

## Addendum — 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (accepted as **already planned**, rank 5 of 10)

The review re-read this proposal against the shipped code and confirms the
chosen shape (**Q1 = A + B**: the hit-charge multiplier as the core rule, the
deflect/critical gate as the juice layer). Four constraints are added below.
None removes or weakens an existing acceptance criterion; they harden the ones
the review judged most likely to make the mechanic feel unfair or illegible.

1. **Resistance, never immunity.** A resisted shot lands at a *reduced* rate —
   one hit point per two connected shots — and never zero, so a wrong loadout is
   **slow and legible rather than a wall**. This is the anti-frustration guard
   for the ring's measured timing budgets (see 4).
2. **Legible within the first seconds, not at the third phase.** The matchup must
   be readable immediately: the boss's **opening cue names the effective and
   resisted weapons**, in the same demonstration vocabulary the hex grants
   already use (body colour plus its own volley, GDD §8.2 capture cycle). The
   deflect and critical feedback families must be distinct **without relying on
   colour** (shape and sound carry the same signal), and the hex detail panel
   keeps publishing the authored `strengths`/`weaknesses` lists.
3. **One rule at the one seam.** The hit-charge multiplier is applied inside the
   single shared player-damage seam (`CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` /
   `MiniBoss.takeDamage`'s caller path) with the bounded per-target ledger in a
   pure module. No per-weapon, per-scene or per-gym branch exists; gym↔game
   parity is asserted by the existing duplicate-body/equivalence guard rather
   than by convention.
4. **Measurement is part of the definition of done.** Both ring-timing lines must
   be re-measured with matchups live — ring 1's **16.2 min** against its 30–90
   window (Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min vs the authored
   40–60 min window, AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X) and ring 2's **48.7 min** against
   60–180 (Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured 48.1 min vs the authored
   90–120 min window, AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5) — plus a same-seed bot batch checked
   against `src/data/experience-targets.json`, with the before/after numbers
   recorded on this item before it advances to `in_review`.

**Interaction with other accepted proposals.** The evolved-weapon proposal
(Weapon evolutions: fuse two active weapon kinds into an evolved weapon,
AH-0MWL7OWPF003E4TP) must resolve an evolved weapon to its **base** weapon id
for matchup purposes, so a fusion pairing can never bypass a hex's authored
strengths and weaknesses; that requirement is carried in its own acceptance
criteria.

# Graze and Danger Multiplier

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 10 of 10 — highest expected enjoyment; direction: create, **High** priority).

## Goal (user story)

As a player threading a dense bullet pattern, I want a near miss to be worth
points and to build a visible multiplier, so that the most skilful thing I do —
flying close to danger — is rewarded rather than merely survived.

## Problem statement

Dodging is currently un-rewarded. Score (GDD §4.5) is a flat per-kill sum plus a
per-level time bonus; there is no multiplier, combo, graze or grade anywhere in
`src/` (verified: no `graze` / `nearMiss` / scoring-`combo` identifiers — the
only `multiplier` hits are bot-tuning and hull speed multipliers). The genre's
strongest retention lever, turning near misses into score, is absent, so a
skilled player and a cautious player are separated only by survival time.

Evidence of the gap:

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_handleCollisions` resolves the player /
  enemy-bullet overlap against a fixed radius with no proximity branch, so the
  band between "hit" and "near miss" is invisible and unpaid.
- The player's collision footprint (≈14 px, `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`
  `PLAYER_HIT_RADIUS`) is already smaller than the 20 px hull art, so a natural
  graze band exists that the player can neither see nor be paid for.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **Graze band.** A graze is recorded when a live enemy bullet or a live enemy
   body passes within `grazeRadius` of the ship's collision centre and outside
   the hit radius, where `grazeRadius = playerHitRadius + GRAZE_BAND` (initial
   `GRAZE_BAND = 12 px`). Judged on the shared collision centre and radius
   helpers, never on sprite bounds. Asteroids and other contact hazards graze
   too — they can kill on contact.
2. **Credit once per pass.** Each hostile object can be grazed once per pass.
   Credit is keyed by a stable per-object id and clears when the object is
   destroyed, when its lifetime expires, or when it leaves the band by more
   than a hysteresis margin (`GRAZE_HYSTERESIS = 4 px`) — so a bullet hovering
   at the band edge cannot farm score.
3. **Danger multiplier.** Five tiers: `×1 → ×1.5 → ×2 → ×3 → ×5`. Each graze
   contributes a fixed amount of tier progress (`GRAZE_TIER_PROGRESS = 1`, so
   the top tier is reached at a tunable count), and inactivity decays the
   multiplier one tier every `GRAZE_DECAY_SECONDS = 2.0`. Kill score is
   multiplied by the current tier, rounded half up, at the existing score seam.
4. **A player hit ends the chain** — the multiplier resets to `×1`, so the risk
   is real and the reward is for *staying* clean.
5. **Legibility.** A spark arc at the nearest point of the grazed object, a
   rising pitch cue per tier, a HUD `DANGER ×N` tacho that drains as the decay
   timer runs, and a distinct flash on tier loss. The signal is never carried
   by colour alone (a shape/pulse difference accompanies each tier).
6. **Purity and parity.** The whole rule lives in one pure module
   (`src/core/graze.ts`) with an explicit tunables record, consumed by the
   shared combat core, so the game and every gym resolve identical values; the
   scene only renders and plays cues.

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It rewards the exact behaviour the game is about, so the inner loop gains a
  second, skill-shaped objective beside survival.
- Close flying becomes a **choice** ("hold the line for a higher tier") rather
  than an accident.
- It gives the leaderboard a skill gap that grinding cannot close, and it is the
  natural scoring substrate for any future run-grade feature.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A pure `src/core/graze.ts` resolves band detection, once-per-object credit,
   hysteresis, tier growth, decay and the score multiplier from an explicit
   tunables record; no scene-local copy exists, and the duplicate-body guard in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` covers the new seam.
2. A live enemy bullet or enemy body entering the band outside the hit radius
   records exactly one graze for that object; leaving and re-entering by less
   than `GRAZE_HYSTERESIS` records none.
3. Kill score is multiplied by the current tier (rounded half up) and the run's
   final score reflects it; grazes award no score beyond tier progress.
4. The multiplier falls one tier per `GRAZE_DECAY_SECONDS` without a graze and
   resets to `×1` on a player hit and at run start.
5. Feedback is present and accessible: tier change reads through shape or pulse
   as well as colour, the HUD shows the tier and its remaining decay, every cue
   respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings and degrades to a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext`.
6. Gym↔game parity: a formation gym exercises detection and tier growth through
   the same shared code path, with a row recorded in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
7. Determinism: the same seed and input trace produce the same graze count and
   score; the rule consumes no RNG of its own.
8. Balance evidence: a same-seed bot batch before/after shows survival,
   `mineralsCollected`, `upgradesSelected` and `avoidableHits` still inside the
   `src/data/experience-targets.json` bands — the expected outcome is **no
   change**, because graze is score-only.
9. Documentation: the normative GDD §4.5 scoring table is amended **when this

A player who threads a bullet pattern now watches a DANGER multiplier climb and

- **Score-only.** Graze never affects damage, movement, lives or drops, so ring

# Weapon evolutions: fuse two active weapon kinds into an evolved weapon

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 8 of 10; direction: create, **Medium** priority).

## Goal (user story)

As a player building a loadout during a run, I want two weapons that work
together to fuse into a visibly different evolved weapon, so that my pickups add
up to an identity I chose rather than a handful of independent streams.

## Problem statement

The sixteen weapons are independent: no rule in `src/utils/weapons.ts` or the
combat core reads a *combination*. A run takes about **two** upgrades (GDD §2.7
target `upgradesSelected 2.00 ± 0.50`), each timed weapon lasts 10 s, and the
hold-full choice offers level-ups of one kind — so a run's build rarely reads as
more than "Cannon plus Spread". The hangar's buy-to-upgrade path raises a single
weapon's level; nothing rewards breadth.

Evidence of the gap:

- `resolveWeaponDefinition` and the shared fire path resolve each active weapon
  in isolation; there is no pairing or combination input anywhere.
- The catalogue is already fully data-driven (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, cadence on
  the shared 16th-note lattice), so a pairing layer is a data + resolver change,
  not a new weapon system.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **Pairings are catalogue data.** A new declarative `evolvesInto` entry on the
   weapon catalogue names, for a **pair** of weapon ids, the evolved weapon id:
   - `ricochet` + `arc` → **Chain Ricochet** — bolts bank off walls *and* hop to
     a second nearby target on each bounce.
   - `cluster` + `mortar` → **Cluster Barrage** — the MIRV warheads leave short
     lingering blasts at their burst points.
   - `spread` + `options` → **Fan Escort** — the orbiting pods fire along the
     ship's heading instead of radially, forming a wide fan.
   Pairings are additive data: a pairing that is absent reproduces today's
   behaviour exactly.
2. **Two evolution tiers, both earned in play (no new economy).**
   - **Field evolution (timed):** while *both* kinds of a pairing are active
     simultaneously — whether from timed drops or ownership — the evolved
     pattern fires for the overlap window. This is reachable in every run with
     any two drops from a pairing, so the mechanic is discoverable immediately.
   - **Permanent evolution (owned):** once both kinds are **permanently owned
     at level ≥ 2** (through the shipped hold-full path, or the hangar's
     buy-to-upgrade levels), the evolved weapon persists for the rest of the run
     and survives the expiry of a timed overlap.
3. **Damage parity.** An evolution changes **pattern, coverage and behaviour
   only** — never the number of damage instances per shot. The boss's 200-hit
   pool (GDD §4.3) and every enemy's hit count therefore stay meaningful, and
   the level-0 output budget (non-cannon weapons ≤ 60 % of the pre-change
   level-0 output, GDD §4.4.2) is respected by the evolved cadence.
4. **Cadence stays on the grid.** The evolved weapon fires on its own
   `(k, n, rotation)` onset pattern on the shared lattice, so upgraded patterns
   still morph only on a bar downbeat and every active weapon stays phase-locked
   (GDD §2.3).
5. **Legibility.** Collecting the second half of a pairing plays a distinct
   "fusion" cue, flashes a HUD badge with the evolved weapon's name and shows
   its icon; expiry of the overlap removes the badge with a matching downbeat
   cue. The badge states which pairing is live so the player can learn the
   recipes from play.
6. **Purity and parity.** The pairing resolver and the evolved-weapon
   resolution live in one pure module consumed by the shared fire path, so the
   game and every weapon gym run identical code.

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It turns a pickup decision into a plan: "I need one more `arc` to get Chain
  Ricochet" is a goal, which is exactly the build identity the experience
  targets say a run currently lacks.
- The timed overlap tier gives an immediate, visible payoff in the very first
  run, while the owned tier gives a long-run target.
- It multiplies the perceived content of sixteen existing weapons without adding
  a weapon slot, a currency or an economy.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A pure pairing resolver (new module beside `src/utils/weapons.ts`) answers,
   for the active/owned weapon set, which evolved weapon (if any) is live, and
   why (field overlap vs owned pair); no scene or gym derives its own answer.
2. Pairings are catalogue data with a validating test: an unknown weapon id in a
   pairing fails loudly; a save/config without pairing data reproduces today's
   behaviour byte-for-byte.
3. **Field tier:** with both kinds of a pairing active, the evolved pattern
   fires; when either expires the evolved weapon stops on the next bar downbeat
   and each half reverts to its own pattern.
4. **Owned tier:** with both kinds permanently owned at level ≥ 2, the evolved
   weapon persists for the run and is cleared by Reset exactly as other owned
   weapons are.
5. **Damage parity:** an automated comparison shows an evolved weapon produces
   no more damage instances per cadence tick than the two halves it replaces;
   the boss still requires 200 hits at every weapon level.
6. **Grid conformance:** every evolved cadence resolves to whole 16th-note
   onsets at `beatBpm`, and pattern morphs occur only on bar downbeats.
7. Feedback: fusion and expiry each read through a distinct cue, a HUD badge
   naming the evolved weapon and an icon, with a shape/text difference that does
   not rely on colour alone; cues respect the shared SFX settings.
8. Gym↔game parity: `GymWeapons` (or a dedicated row) fires every shipped
   pairing through the shared code path, with a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
9. Determinism: same seed and input trace produce the same firing trace.
10. Balance evidence: a same-seed bot batch shows `survivalSeconds`,
    `levelReached` and `avoidableHits` inside the experience-target bands, and
    the ring-timing harness re-measured (an evolution that shortens ring 1 below
    its window is a tuning input, not a blocker).
11. Documentation: the GDD §4.4 catalogue section gains the pairing table **when
    this lands** (the proposal is already recorded in GDD §8.3), plus
    `docs/weaponBalanceDocs`-style test coverage for the table.
12. The full project test suite passes (through the test skill).

## Impact

A player who collects a second weapon that pairs with their first now sees the
two fuse into a named, visibly different weapon, so a run's pickups add up to a
build the player chose rather than a longer list of guns.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **No new economy and no new slot.** Evolutions consume the existing six shared
  slots and the existing hold-full/hangar level paths; nothing is purchasable.
- **Pattern, not power.** Evolutions must not raise damage per tick; the
  balance risk is coverage, not DPS, and the acceptance test above pins it.
- **Authored, not combinatorial.** Start with three pairings; the mechanism
  supports more, but each pairing is a balance-tested content unit.
- **One resolver.** Pairing logic never appears in a scene, a gym or a
  bot-decision module (bot decisions read the resolved active set).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` (new) + tests — pairings and resolution.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — declarative pairing data and evolved definitions.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / the shared fire path — one resolved
  active-weapon read.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/icons.ts`, HUD — fusion badge/cue.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — the parity row.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 and §8.3.

## Related work

- GDD §2.3 (shared beat lattice), §4.4 (weapon catalogue and the level-0 output
  budget), §4.4.2 (weapon strength budget), §4.3 (boss hit pool).
- Hangar buy-to-upgrade permanent levels (AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU) — the owned tier
  reads those levels.
- Hangar power-up ownership: no path creates a power-up's first permanent level
  row (AH-0MWKT12BT001106T) — sibling work on the ownership model.
- Classic-arcade arsenal research (`docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`) —
  the pairing layer is the natural home for future researched weapons.

# Anomaly (elite) enemies and wave twists

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 7 of 10; direction: create, **Medium** priority).

## Goal (user story)

As a player working through the campaign's waves, I want some waves to field a
visibly special enemy with an extra behaviour and a real reward, so that wave 60
does not feel like wave 6 with more bodies.

## Problem statement

The campaign is 100 waves (ten per level) built from a fixed archetype roster
with escalating counts, and difficulty rises on exactly two axes — enemy count
(1.00× → 2.00×) and a falling per-kill drop chance (GDD §4.6). After the
classic-arcade debut in level 6, novelty is carried almost entirely by density,
so later waves read as the same formations scaled up.

Evidence of the gap:

- No elite, anomaly, champion or variant identifier exists in `src/` today.
- Archetypes are already per-enemy CSV data (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with
  `movementClass`/`attackClass`, so a variant axis is a data change on an
  existing spawn path.
- The bounded-behaviour precedent already exists: the hex personalities
  implement exactly two shared combat mechanics (a projectile-slowing `nebula`
  and a reinforcement-summoning `summoner`) once in the shared combat core
  (`src/scenes/core/hexPersonalityMechanics.ts`), proving the pattern is cheap.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **One elite per wave, authored or seeded.** A wave may author one **elite**
   spawn; when a wave authors none, a seeded budget grants an elite on a
   tunable share of waves (initial `ELITE_WAVE_CHANCE = 0.15`). **Level 1 never
   spawns an elite** — onboarding and the experience-target baseline stay
   untouched.
2. **A variant of a counted archetype, never a new entity.** An elite is the
   same archetype with: a distinct aura + rim treatment (visibly different
   silhouette treatment, not colour alone), `+ELITE_BONUS_HP` (1–3, data-driven
   per archetype) and **one** extra behaviour drawn from a small bounded set:
   - **splitter** — on death it releases two ordinary children of its own
     archetype (reusing the shared spawn seam the asteroid/harvester spawners
     use);
   - **reinforced** — it spawns behind the shipped force-field layer at one
     extra field hit (reusing `enemyForceFieldHits` and the shared bubble
     visuals);
   - **volatile** — on death it leaves a short-lived radial burst of its own
     bullets (reusing the boss pulse/minion vocabulary and the existing enemy
     bullet seam).
3. **Wave accounting is unchanged.** An elite is a counted wave enemy, so a wave
   still clears only when its ships are destroyed; it is never an asteroid-style
   non-counted hazard and can never stall or short-circuit a wave.
4. **A real, visible reward.** An elite always drops from the shared pool and
   carries a guaranteed **mineral bump** (2–4, level-scaled through the existing
   `levelScaling` curve). Its drop is announced by a distinct death cue so the
   payoff is legible at a glance.
5. **Announced, never a surprise.** The wave's opening cue names the elite and a
   short-lived `ELITE` tag tracks the hull while it lives, so the player can
   prioritise it — this is the decision the mechanic exists to create.
6. **Arcade-safe.** Elites are authored/off by default in the arcade campaign's
   first fields until the bot batch clears (see AC9); the hex ring's boss
   deployments are unaffected (no elite spawns there).

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It adds cheap novelty exactly where the game is most repetitive, at the
  moment-to-moment scale the player feels most often.
- A priority target makes a familiar formation a decision again: "kill the
  splitter first or lose the gap".
- The guaranteed reward gives a wave-clear plan a visible payoff, improving the
  mineral cadence that the middle loop depends on.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An elite variant is data-driven (CSV/config column plus a bounded behaviour
   id), validated loudly: an unknown behaviour id or an elite on an uncounted
   hazard fails at load, not at spawn.
2. Level 1 never spawns an elite; a wave that authors one spawns exactly one;
   the seeded budget path is deterministic given the run seed.
3. An elite is a counted wave enemy: the wave clears only when it is destroyed,
   it survives the wave-timeout carry-over rule exactly as an ordinary enemy,
   and it can never be an `asteroid`/`lane-traffic` non-counted hazard.
4. Each of the three behaviours works through a shared seam (no bespoke
   per-archetype copy): children spawn through the shared spawn path, the extra
   field hit through `enemyForceFieldHits`, the death burst through the shared
   enemy-bullet seam; a behaviour absent from the data reproduces today's
   behaviour byte-for-byte.
5. Reward: an elite always drops from the shared pool and pays the level-scaled
   guaranteed mineral bump, with a distinct death cue that respects the shared
   SFX settings.
6. Legibility: the elite's aura, tag and opening-wave announcement read without
   relying on colour alone; the tag disappears exactly when the elite dies.
7. Gym↔game parity: `GymFodderEnemies` (or the level gym) spawns every elite
   behaviour through the same code path as the game, with a `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
   row.
8. Determinism: same seed + same wave ⇒ same elite, same position, same reward
   (the seeded budget consumes the run-seeded stream in a documented order, and
   the campaign variety/signature audit is unaffected because an elite does not
   change an archetype *set*).
9. Balance evidence: a same-seed bot batch shows `survivalSeconds`,
   `mineralsCollected` and `avoidableHits` inside the experience-target bands;
   the level-scaling table in `docs/BALANCING.md` is re-measured with elites on
   and the result recorded on this item before the shipped default is raised
   above zero.
10. Documentation: GDD §4.1/§4.6 and the new §8.3 entry, plus `docs/BALANCING.md`
    with the measured before/after.
11. The full project test suite passes (through the test skill).

## Impact

A player clearing a familiar formation now spots a lit, tougher anomaly with a
guaranteed payoff and has to decide whether to break formation to kill it first,
so mid-campaign waves carry a decision instead of only more bodies.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Bounded content.** Three behaviours maximum for the first slice; each is a
  re-use of a shipped seam, and none may need a new entity class.
- **Ships only.** Elites are variants of counted archetypes, never hazards, so
  wave-completion logic and the sequencer's clearability invariant are
  untouched.
- **Onboarding frozen.** Level 1 is elite-free and the level-1 identity
  transform is preserved.
- **No new persistence.** Elite choice is derived from the run seed and the wave
  data; nothing is written to any save.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` + `src/core/configTypes.ts` — the variant columns
  (`eliteBehaviour`, `eliteBonusHp`).
- `src/waves/` (planner) — the seeded elite budget and per-wave authoring.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` spawn path, `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — aura/tag
  and the death behaviour hook.
- `src/scenes/core/hexPersonalityMechanics.ts` — the precedent seam to mirror
  for a bounded shared-mechanic set.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — parity row.
- `docs/BALANCING.md`, GDD §4.1, §4.6, §8.3.

## Related work

- GDD §4.1 (archetypes and force fields), §4.2 (wave structures and the
  wave-timeout carry-over rule), §4.6 (the two difficulty axes).
- Hex variety: personalities, contracts and ring landmarks (AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG)
  — the shipped bounded-mechanics precedent.
- Enemy roster docs guard (`src/enemyRosterDocs.test.ts`) — the variant axis
  must be added to the roster documentation it validates.
